text:
elaine: quick sanity check on the new pastel-13b bringup — ran int6 & int8 on chat + longform slices, plus KV-cache microbench. TL;DR: int6 ≈ 1.7x cheaper than int8, but we see ~3–4% quality drop on high-exactness slices.

devin: thanks — can you drop the raw numbers for unit cost and latency?

elaine: sure. summary per 1k tokens: int8 ~ $1.20, int6 ~ $0.70. p50/p95 (chat): int8 120ms / 210ms, int6 130ms / 225ms. longform tail: int8 480ms, int6 510ms.

kai: how about hallucination/precision signals on the eval slices? any concentrated regressions?

elaine: hallucination (numeric/factual) up ~4% absolute on the exactness slice set (n=1.2k). retrieval-heavy prompts see bigger drift — answer fidelity down ~6% when KV cache hit < 0.2.

marta: product POV — 4% QA drop is borderline for GTN flows that require deterministic answers. We should consider selective routing.

devin: proposing a routing policy: default int6, route to int8 when a precision detector flags the prompt as high-risk. rough blended cost calc: if 30% of traffic routed to int8, blended unit cost ~ $0.82 per 1k tokens (vs $1.20 baseline if all int8).

elaine: classifier proto is at model-signal/precision-detector (micro F1 0.86 on dev). sample routing config:
```
route:
  - match: precision_detector >= 0.8
    model: pastel-13b-int8
  - else:
    model: pastel-13b-int6
```
This keeps latency impact small while protecting high-precision queries.

ops-bot: Canary deploy completed: pastel-13b-int6 -> dedicated pool "coldstart-1" (5% traffic). Logs: <https://redwood/logs/deploy/1714999999>

marta: good. next steps: run 24h replay/live-slice checks against GTN top-50 queries, capture QA delta, p95, and token spend. if any user-visible regressions >2% we rollback.

devin: I'll create a short cost projection for low/medium/high traffic tiers and model the SLA risk. ETA: EOD.

elaine: added a concise scorecard in sheets: unit-cost, FPQA-drop, p95 latency, cache-hit delta. link: <https://redwood/sheets/pastel-13b-onboard>

devin: ack, will sync with Solutions tomorrow to scope the routing rollout and GTN test. :thumbsup:
